newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power rises with cooler weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power rises with cooler weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were steady to higher again on Tuesday, as slightly cooler temperatures and stronger natural gas prices gave support to the market.

Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to hover about two to eight degrees Fahrenheit below normal this week, with some sleet and snow possible in parts of Tennessee and northern Alabama late Tuesday or early Wednesday.
By the weekend, temperatures are forecast to dip to 10-20 degrees F below normal.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Wednesday were mostly higher in the $20.00-21.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Monday's $17.00-20.00 trading range.
In pursuit of stronger gas prices, traders said early firm, peak deals into TVA were done as high as $26.00, but as gas prices spiraled downward TVA prices were heard as low as $18.50.
For next week delivery, TVA prices were talked in the $22.50-25.00 range.
Firm, off-peak electricity prices in northern TVA for Wednesday were assessed in the $10.00-13.00 range, traders said.
Prices at the Georgia/Florida border for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Wednesday delivery were talked steady to up slightly in the $24.00-26.00 range.
Firm, off-peak power for Wednesday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally lower at $13.00.

In Florida, where daytime temperature highs are anywhere from the 50s to the 80s and lows of 40s are being reached in the north, firm, peak electricity prices on a 16-hour schedule for Wednesday were around $26.50-27.50 per MWh.

As the cooler weather arrived, natural gas prices soared above the $4 per million British thermal units mark in the Midcontinent and west Texas markets. Most Gulf values were pegged in the $3.76-3.81 area, up more than 30 cents from Monday.
